outcome: The stated conjecture (KL polynomial values at 1 = Jordan-Hölder multiplicities of simple modules in Verma modules, for complex semisimple Lie groups/algebras) was proved independently by Beilinson-Bernstein and by Brylinski-Kashiwara in 1981, long before the 26 January 2024 frozen revision; nothing in the 2024-2026 window changes this. Substantial 2024-2026 activity exists on distinct, related problems in the same corner of representation theory (the Combinatorial Invariance Conjecture for KL polynomials, the p-adic KL hypothesis for GL(n), and empirical/computational studies of KL polynomials), none of which is a case of or a restatement of the bullet's stated conjecture. One genuine, well-documented AI event was found, but it belongs to a different, unrelated conjecture in a 2024 paper about KL polynomials generally, not to the classical conjecture in this bullet.
summary: The bullet's stated conjecture is the classical 1979 Kazhdan-Lusztig conjecture relating KL polynomial values at q=1 to composition-series multiplicities of simple modules inside Verma modules for complex semisimple Lie algebras/groups. This was proved in 1981, independently, by Beilinson-Bernstein and by Brylinski-Kashiwara (confirmed via the Wikipedia article on Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials, which states both proofs and that they launched geometric representation theory), so the correct status given the frozen-revision rule is open_stale, exactly as the triage pass concluded. I then searched specifically for 2024-2026 activity to check whether anything in the window bears on this bullet regardless. I found three clusters of genuine activity, none of which is in scope: (1) the Combinatorial Invariance Conjecture (Lusztig-Dyer), a distinct conjecture about whether KL polynomials depend only on Bruhat-interval isomorphism type -- Barkley and Gaetz proved it for elementary intervals (Math. Annalen 2025), and other 2024-2026 papers proved parabolic and lower-interval cases (BBDVW conjecture, arXiv 2412.10256); (2) a 2025 proof of the p-adic KL hypothesis for GL(n) (arXiv 2510.09788), a p-adic analogue over a different ground field; (3) 'Big data approach to Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials' (Lacabanne-Tubbenhauer-Vaz, arXiv 2412.01283, J. Experimental Math. 2026), an empirical/computational study of KL polynomial coefficients for symmetric groups up to 11 strands. This third paper is the one AI-relevant item found in the whole search: its acknowledgments state 'In this work, we utilized ChatGPT for coding, proofreading, generating conjectures, and assisting with proof development' (ai_role would be none for this alone, per the rule that proofreading/coding/strategy-suggestion is not AI-producing-the-mathematics), and a later remark (added in v2/v3, and per arXiv's own version-comment metadata and the paper's GitHub repository dtubbenhauer/kldata) states that on 26 June 2026 Eivind Otto Hjelle contacted the authors with a proof of the paper's Conjecture 6.4 -- a closed-form formula P_{e,w}(q) = (1+q+...+q^l)^{k-1} for KL polynomials of a specific family of permutations -- generated by 'ChatGPT 5.5 Pro', and the authors state 'We have reviewed the generated argument and were unable to find any mistakes in the logic.' This is a real, well-corroborated (arXiv abs-page comments, the paper body, and the GitHub README all agree) AI-generated-proof event, but it is entirely out of scope for this bullet: Conjecture 6.4 is the paper's own empirically-discovered conjecture about a specific closed-form family of KL polynomial values, not a case of or a variant on the classical Kazhdan-Lusztig conjecture stated in the bullet (multiplicities in Verma modules at q=1 for general semisimple Lie algebras). I record it here only to show the search was thorough and to explain the one 'AI + Kazhdan-Lusztig' item that surfaces in any broad search of this area; it does not move this problem's status. No result found anywhere restates, extends, or contradicts the 1981 theorem itself.
competing_reading: One could argue the field/subfield header ('Algebra / Representation theory') is broad enough that any KL-polynomial result, including the Conjecture 6.4 closed-form formula or the Combinatorial Invariance results, should count as informing this bullet, since they concern 'Kazhdan-Lusztig' objects. I reject this: per the scope rule (§3.1), a related problem is one obtained by changing the stated question (different conjecture, different objects), not restricting it, and Conjecture 6.4 and the Combinatorial Invariance Conjecture are each a different mathematical statement from the multiplicity-conjecture in the bullet, sharing only the name 'Kazhdan-Lusztig' and the underlying polynomials as a common object of study.
what_would_settle_it: Nothing further is needed to settle the open_stale classification of the bullet itself; it was proved in 1981. What would change this record's characterization of the searched activity is if a future source showed that the Combinatorial Invariance Conjecture, once fully proved, implies a strengthening or reproof of the 1981 multiplicity theorem via a different route -- but no source found suggests any logical connection of that kind.
